overview: This bill aims to better connect young parents and parents-to-be who have been in foster care with home visiting programs, in which nurses or trained workers visit families to support healthy pregnancies and early child development. It adds this goal to the John H. Chafee program, which funds state services for youth transitioning out of foster care, and links it to the federal Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program. Each state's governor would have to certify that eligible youth in the program receive information about home visiting services in their state. States could also use Chafee funds for tailored case management and coordination of resources for expectant and parenting youth. The changes would take effect one year after enactment. As of May 11, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say young parents who grew up in foster care often lack family support, and steering them toward proven home visiting services can help both them and their children.
against: Critics say the bill mainly requires states to share information and certify processes, without new money, so it may do little to expand services where home visiting slots are already limited.
